lines.raw: A **provider** is anyone who gives healthcare.
lines.say: A provider is anyone who gives healthcare.

lines.raw: The important thing to remember: a provider is **not only a doctor**.
lines.say: The important thing to remember: a provider is not only a doctor.

lines.raw: It can be a **person** or an **organization**.
lines.say: It can be a person or an organization.

lines.raw: Who. 👩‍⚕️ Individual provider (a person): Doctors, nurses, physiotherapists, dentists, pharmacists. 🏥 Organization provider (a facility): Hospitals, clinics, labs, nursing homes, pharmacies.
lines.say: Who. 👩‍⚕️ Individual provider (a person): Doctors, nurses, physiotherapists, dentists, pharmacists. 🏥 Organization provider (a facility): Hospitals, clinics, labs, nursing homes, pharmacies.

lines.raw: One visit, both kinds of provider.
lines.say: One visit, both kinds of provider.

lines.raw: When Emily sees Dr. Patel at Sunrise Family Clinic, **both** are providers on the same claim: Dr. Patel (a **person**) did the work, and the clinic (an **organization**) sends the bill and receives the money.
lines.say: When Emily sees Doctor Patel at Sunrise Family Clinic, both are providers on the same claim: Doctor Patel (a person) did the work, and the clinic (an organization) sends the bill and receives the money.

lines.raw: On the claim, Dr. Patel is the **rendering provider** (who gave the care) and the clinic is the **billing provider** (who gets paid).
lines.say: On the claim, Doctor Patel is the rendering provider (who gave the care) and the clinic is the billing provider (who gets paid).

lines.raw: More on these roles below.
lines.say: More on these roles below.

lines.raw: Every provider has an ID.
lines.say: Every provider has an I D.

lines.raw: Names can be spelled many ways ("Dr. R.
lines.say: Names can be spelled many ways ("Doctor R.

lines.raw: Sharma", "Ramesh Sharma MD", "Sharma Ramesh"), so claims identify providers with **ID numbers** instead.
lines.say: Sharma", "Ramesh Sharma M D", "Sharma Ramesh"), so claims identify providers with I D numbers instead.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **NPI** (National Provider Identifier). What it is: A 10-digit number every US provider gets from **CMS** (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the US government's health agency). It never changes, even if the doctor moves. Nepal comparison: A doctor's **NMC registration number** from the Nepal Medical Council.
lines.say: N P I (National Provider Identifier). What it is: A 10-digit number every U S provider gets from C M S (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, the U S government's health agency). It never changes, even if the doctor moves. Nepal comparison: A doctor's N M C registration number from the Nepal Medical Council.

lines.raw: **TIN** (Tax Identification Number). What it is: A **9-digit** tax number of the business that receives the money. Usually written as `XX-XXXXXXX`, for example `12-3456789`. Nepal comparison: A hospital's **PAN number**, printed on every bill. Also 9 digits!
lines.say: T I N (Tax Identification Number). What it is: A 9-digit tax number of the business that receives the money. Usually written as X X XXXXXXX, for example 1 2 dash 3 4 5 6 7 8 9. Nepal comparison: A hospital's P A N number, printed on every bill. Also 9 digits!

lines.raw: **Taxonomy code**. What it is: A 10-character code for the provider's type and specialty. Example: `207Q00000X` = Family Medicine. Nepal comparison: The specialty written on the doctor's nameboard: "MD, Internal Medicine".
lines.say: Taxonomy code. What it is: A 10-character code for the provider's type and specialty. Example: 2 0 7 Q 0 0 0 0 0 X = Family Medicine. Nepal comparison: The specialty written on the doctor's nameboard: "M D, Internal Medicine".

lines.say: Type 1 N P I.

lines.say: Given to a person (individual provider): Doctor Patel has her own N P I.

lines.say: Type 2 N P I.

lines.say: Given to an organization (facility): the hospital or clinic has its own N P I.

lines.raw: Roles: who did what?
lines.say: Roles: who did what?

lines.raw: A claim can mention several providers.
lines.say: A claim can mention several providers.

lines.raw: Each one has a **role**.
lines.say: Each one has a role.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Rendering** (servicing). Meaning: The person who actually performed the service. Example: Dr. Patel, who examined Emily.
lines.say: Rendering (servicing). Meaning: The person who actually performed the service. Example: Doctor Patel, who examined Emily.

lines.raw: **Billing**. Meaning: The person or organization that sends the claim and receives the money. Example: Sunrise Family Clinic, where Dr. Patel works.
lines.say: Billing. Meaning: The person or organization that sends the claim and receives the money. Example: Sunrise Family Clinic, where Doctor Patel works.

lines.raw: **Referring**. Meaning: The provider who sent the patient to another provider. Example: Emily's family doctor sends her to a surgeon.
lines.say: Referring. Meaning: The provider who sent the patient to another provider. Example: Emily's family doctor sends her to a surgeon.

lines.raw: **Ordering**. Meaning: The provider who asked for a test or item. Example: Dr. Patel orders a blood test from a lab.
lines.say: Ordering. Meaning: The provider who asked for a test or item. Example: Doctor Patel orders a blood test from a lab.

lines.raw: **Attending**. Meaning: The main doctor responsible for a hospital patient (on UB-04). Example: The surgeon in charge of Emily's hospital stay.
lines.say: Attending. Meaning: The main doctor responsible for a hospital patient (on U B 04). Example: The surgeon in charge of Emily's hospital stay.

lines.raw: Rendering vs. billing, in everyday words.
lines.say: Rendering versus billing, in everyday words.

lines.raw: A chef cooks your food (**rendering**), but you pay the restaurant (**billing**).
lines.say: A chef cooks your food (rendering), but you pay the restaurant (billing).

lines.raw: Dr. Patel examined Emily, but the money goes to the clinic that employs her.
lines.say: Doctor Patel examined Emily, but the money goes to the clinic that employs her.

lines.raw: Roles in a Nepali hospital.
lines.say: Roles in a Nepali hospital.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: Ram sees **Dr. Shrestha** in the OPD.
lines.say: Ram sees Doctor Shrestha in the O P D.

lines.raw: Dr. Shrestha is the **rendering** provider.
lines.say: Doctor Shrestha is the rendering provider.

lines.raw: Ram pays the **hospital cash counter**, not Dr. Shrestha.
lines.say: Ram pays the hospital cash counter, not Doctor Shrestha.

lines.raw: The hospital is the **billing** provider.
lines.say: The hospital is the billing provider.

lines.raw: Its PAN number is on the receipt.
lines.say: Its P A N number is on the receipt.

lines.raw: When Ram claims from his insurer, the receipt with the hospital's **PAN** and the doctor's **NMC number** helps prove the bill is genuine.
lines.say: When Ram claims from his insurer, the receipt with the hospital's P A N and the doctor's N M C number helps prove the bill is genuine.

lines.raw: Dr. Shrestha writes "refer to ENT".
lines.say: Doctor Shrestha writes "refer to E N T".

lines.raw: The ENT doctor Ram sees next was **referred** by Dr. Shrestha.
lines.say: The E N T doctor Ram sees next was referred by Doctor Shrestha.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: SSF only pays hospitals that are **listed (empanelled)** with SSF.
lines.say: S S F only pays hospitals that are listed (empanelled) with S S F.

lines.raw: This is just like a US "network".
lines.say: This is just like a U S "network".

lines.raw: If Sita goes to a hospital that is **not** SSF-listed, SSF will normally not pay that hospital directly.
lines.say: If Sita goes to a hospital that is not S S F listed, S S F will normally not pay that hospital directly.

lines.raw: In the claim to SSF, the hospital is the billing provider and the treating doctor is recorded on the visit.
lines.say: In the claim to S S F, the hospital is the billing provider and the treating doctor is recorded on the visit.

lines.raw: In-network vs. out-of-network.
lines.say: In-network versus out-of-network.

lines.raw: US insurance companies sign contracts with many doctors and hospitals.
lines.say: U S insurance companies sign contracts with many doctors and hospitals.

lines.raw: These contracted providers form the insurer's **network**.
lines.say: These contracted providers form the insurer's network.

lines.raw: They agree to accept **discounted prices**.
lines.say: They agree to accept discounted prices.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Contract with insurer? In-network: Yes. Out-of-network: No.
lines.say: Contract with insurer? In-network: Yes. Out-of-network: No.

lines.raw: Price. In-network: Agreed discounted price. Out-of-network: Full price, or whatever the insurer decides.
lines.say: Price. In-network: Agreed discounted price. Out-of-network: Full price, or whatever the insurer decides.

lines.raw: What patient pays. In-network: Less. Out-of-network: More, or sometimes everything.
lines.say: What patient pays. In-network: Less. Out-of-network: More, or sometimes everything.

lines.raw: Who sends the claim? In-network: The provider. Out-of-network: Often the **patient** pays first and claims it back (like Ram).
lines.say: Who sends the claim? In-network: The provider. Out-of-network: Often the patient pays first and claims it back (like Ram).

lines.raw: Nepal SSF comparison. In-network: SSF-listed hospital. Out-of-network: Hospital not listed with SSF.
lines.say: Nepal S S F comparison. In-network: S S F listed hospital. Out-of-network: Hospital not listed with S S F.

lines.raw: Primary Care Physician (PCP).
lines.say: Primary Care Physician (P C P).

lines.raw: Some US plans (HMOs) make each member choose a **PCP**, a regular family doctor who is the first stop for every problem and who must **refer** the patient before they can see a specialist.
lines.say: Some U S plans (H M O's) make each member choose a P C P, a regular family doctor who is the first stop for every problem and who must refer the patient before they can see a specialist.

lines.raw: This rule is **not for emergencies**: in an emergency, patients can skip the PCP and go straight to the **emergency room (ER)**.
lines.say: This rule is not for emergencies: in an emergency, patients can skip the P C P and go straight to the emergency room (E R).

lines.raw: Nepal's government health insurance has a similar idea: you register at a first service point and need a referral for bigger hospitals.
lines.say: Nepal's government health insurance has a similar idea: you register at a first service point and need a referral for bigger hospitals.

lines.raw: Data tip.
lines.say: Data tip.

lines.raw: One hospital can have several NPIs (for its main building, rehab unit, outpatient clinic...).
lines.say: One hospital can have several N P I's (for its main building, rehab unit, outpatient clinic...).

lines.raw: One NPI should only ever belong to one provider.
lines.say: One N P I should only ever belong to one provider.

lines.raw: When totals by provider look odd, check whether you need to group multiple NPIs together.
lines.say: When totals by provider look odd, check whether you need to group multiple N P I's together.

lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: A provider can be a **person** (doctor, nurse) or an **organization** (hospital, clinic, lab).
lines.say: A provider can be a person (doctor, nurse) or an organization (hospital, clinic, lab).

lines.say: N P I = 10-digit provider I D (like an N M C number).

lines.raw: TIN = tax ID (like a PAN number).
lines.say: T I N = tax I D (like a P A N number).

lines.raw: Rendering = who did the work.
lines.say: Rendering = who did the work.

lines.raw: Billing = who gets paid.
lines.say: Billing = who gets paid.

lines.raw: Referring sends the patient; ordering asks for a test; attending leads a hospital stay.
lines.say: Referring sends the patient; ordering asks for a test; attending leads a hospital stay.

lines.raw: In-network providers have a contract with the insurer, like SSF-listed hospitals in Nepal.
